\"is_published\": true, \"raw_source_name\": \"Social Cognitive and Affective Neuroscience\", \"raw_type\": \"journal-article\"}, \"abstract\": \"Activation in frontopolar cortex (FPC; BA 10) has been associated both with attending to mental states and with integrating multiple mental relations. However, few previous studies have manipulated both of these cognitive processes, precluding a clear functional distinction among regions within FPC. To address this issue, we developed an fMRI task that combined mentalizing and relational integration processes. Participants saw blocks of single words and performed one of three judgments: how pleasant or unpleasant they found each word (Self condition), how a specific friend would evaluate the pleasantness of the word (Other condition), or the difference between their own pleasantness judgment and that of their friend (Relational condition). We found that medial FPC was modulated by Other relative to Self judgments, consistent with a role in mentalizing. Lateral FPC was significantly activated during Relational compared to Self judgements, suggesting that this region is particularly involved in relational integration. The results point to a strong functional dissociation between medial and lateral FPC. In addition, the data demonstrate a role for lateral FPC in the social domain, provided that the task requires the integration of one's preferences with those of others.\"}, {\"id\": \"https://openalex.org/W2143775381\", \"doi\": null, \"title\": \"Constitutional Value Judgments and Interpretive Theory Choice\", \"publication_year\": 2012, \"type\": \"article\", \"cited_by_count\": 0, \"open_access\": {\"is_oa\": true, \"oa_status\": \"green\", \"oa_url\": \"https://ir.law.fsu.edu/lr/vol40/iss2/2\", \"any_repository_has_fulltext\": true}, \"primary_location\": {\"id\": \"pmh:oai:ir.law.fsu.edu:lr-1008\", \"doi\": null, \"is_oa\": true, \"landing_page_url\": \"https://ir.law.fsu.edu/lr/vol40/iss2/2\", \"pdf_url\": \"https://ir.law.fsu.edu/lr/vol40/iss2/2\", \"source\": {\"id\": \"https://openalex.org/S4377196785\", \"display_name\": \"Scholorship Repository - Florida State University College of Law (Florida State University)\", \"issn_l\": null, \"issn\": null, \"is_oa\": false, \"is_in_doaj\": false, \"is_core\": false, \"listed_in\": [], \"host_organization\": \"https://openalex.org/I103163165\", \"host_organization_name\": \"Florida State University\", \"host_organization_lineage\": [\"https://openalex.org/I103163165\"], \"host_organization_lineage_names\": [], \"type\": \"repository\"}, \"license\": null, \"license_id\": null, \"version\": \"submittedVersion\", \"is_accepted\": false, \"is_published\": false, \"raw_source_name\": \"Florida State University Law Review\", \"raw_type\": \"text\"}, \"abstract\": \"How am I to obey a rule?\\\" If this is not a question about causes, then it is about the justification for my following the rule the way I do. This estimate may be derived from visual velocity and/or vestibular acceleration signals. Importantly, these senses in isolation are ill-equipped to provide accurate estimates, and thus visuo-vestibular integration is an imperative. After a summary of the visual and vestibular pathways involved, the crux of this review focuses on the human and theoretical approaches that have outlined a normative account of cue combination in behavior and neurons, as well as on the systems neuroscience efforts that are searching for its neural implementation. We then highlight a contemporary frontier in our state of knowledge: understanding how velocity cues with time-varying reliabilities are integrated into an evolving position estimate over prolonged time periods. Further, we discuss how the brain builds internal models inferring when cues ought to be integrated versus segregated-a process of causal inference. Lastly, we suggest that the study of spatial navigation has not yet addressed its initial condition: self-location.\"}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "69cba1cdf2b0643e94d15cc36c8adb88e2d7dfb82036f9007690dea3617343d4", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "unassigned_problem", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.1111/acps.70047", "doi:10.1093/scan/nsq033", "doi:10.1146/annurev-psych-021021-103038", "openalex:W4416440091", "openalex:W2162786749", "openalex:W2143775381", "openalex:W3199956788"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.1111/acps.70047", "https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdfdirect/10.1111/acps.70047", "https://doi.org/10.1093/scan/nsq033", "https://academic.oup.com/scan/article-pdf/6/3/260/27106114/nsq033.pdf", "https://ir.law.fsu.edu/lr/vol40/iss2/2", "https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-psych-021021-103038"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
